newsitem.title: FRANCE: Writer Julien Green quits French Academy - report.
newsitem.headline: Writer Julien Green quits French Academy - report.

text.p: U.S. writer Julien Green resigned on Thursday from the prestigious French Academy, saying he had no time for honours, French television reported.

France-2 news reported that Green, 96, made the announcement that he was quitting the institution in an open letter to perpetual secretary Maurice Druon and to his peers. There was no immediate confirmation of the report.
In the letter, the doyen of the society set up by Cardinal Richelieu in 1635, described himself as "exclusively" American and stated that "honours do not interest me at all, whatever they are".
Members of the academy, whose main task is defending the purity of the French language, in principle cannot resign from the institution.
But Green, who was elected in 1971 to succeed Francois Mauriac, said he would not go back on his decision.
Born to American parents in Paris in September 1900, Green studied at a lycee in the capital and at the University of Virginia. He settled in France in 1945.

His largely autobiographical works, translated into a dozen languages, have been published in France in the coveted Pleiade collection by Gallimard (seven volumes) and include "Mont-Cinere", "Adrienne Mesurat", and "Leviathan".
Honours showered on Green include the Legion of Honour, France's highest award.
